:::{#thm-collision-entropy-at-most-entropy}
#### The collision entropy is at most the Shannon entropy

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) that takes finitely many values.
Then the [collision entropy](#def-renyi-entropy) is at most the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy):

$$H_2(X) \le \entropyf{X}.$$

The two are equal exactly when all the values that $X$ takes with positive probability are equally likely.

:::

::: proof

Write $\P(X)$ for the [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) evaluated at $X$.
The function $-\log$ is [strictly convex](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-convex-function), <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
so Jensen's inequality gives

$$\E{-\log \P(X)} \ge -\log \E{\P(X)},$$

with equality exactly when $\P(X)$ is constant. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
The left side is $\entropyf{X}$.
The right side is $H_2(X)$ by its definition.
The function $\P(X)$ is constant exactly when every value that $X$ takes with positive probability has that same probability.

:::
